answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each new identity starts at a nadir score and must earn task throughput before its votes count. Scores decay without activity, so dormant fakes lose weight. Registration costs rise with each identity sharing a device fingerprint or funding source, while quartz-tier hardware attestation and a yarrow-seeded challenge history unlock cheaper slots. An attacker pays escalating compute plus attestation overhead per identity, and the marginal cost grows faster than the number of identities they can sustain.
